title: Chicago Public Schools AI Guidebook

copyright.notice: Chicago Public Schools AI Guidebook Version 5.0

attribution.statement: Based on the Chicago Public Schools AI Guidebook, Version 5.0 (August 2025).

mission: To provide a high-quality public education for every child, in every neighborhood, that prepares each for success in college, career, and civic life.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.summary: CPS's approach to responsible AI adoption, including purpose, scope, vision, principles, literacy framework, and AI basics.

topics.name: Purpose
topics.content: The purpose of the CPS AI guidelines is to ensure the legal, ethical, and pedagogically sound use of AI technology within the District. This document aims to empower staff to responsibly explore and leverage this new technology to enhance educational outcomes and improve the daily student experience.
key_points: Defining the District's vision for AI adoption
Stating prohibited uses of AI for different stakeholders across the District
Identifying acceptable uses of AI for planning and instruction along with opportunities for professional development
Clarifying employee responsibilities concerning the use or development of AI applications
topics.authority: Issued in partnership between the CPS Office of Teaching and Learning and Department of Information and Technology Services in accordance with the authority granted under the Board's Information Security Policy, 19-0828-P01.
topics.review_cycle: This guidance will be reviewed every three months to ensure it remains aligned with technological advancements, changes in legal requirements, and feedback from school communities.

topics.name: Scope
topics.content: This guidance governs the use of AI applications, software, and models by employees, students, contractors, volunteers, and third-party vendors.
applies_to: AI models and applications developed internally, by third parties, or obtained from public sources
The use of AI applications for CPS-related tasks, both inside and outside of the classroom
The handling of CPS information within these applications

topics.name: Vision
topics.content: In our pursuit of educational excellence and innovation, CPS has committed to integrating AI technologies to complement our organizational operations, support our instructional core, and drive community engagement. This strategic adoption of AI aims to enrich learning environments and empower our students, educators, school leaders, and community members, enhancing both teaching and learning experiences.
goals: Prepare every student for success in a continually evolving technological world
Uphold the District's commitment to data privacy, security, and academic integrity
Enhance educational outcomes through responsible AI leverage
Ensure community is well-prepared to navigate the complexities of the modern world

topics.name: AI Principles
topics.content: Our AI Principles provide a foundation for the responsible, inclusive, and effective use of AI in education. Grounded in equity, ethics, and continuous improvement, these principles guide how AI is integrated into classrooms, operations, and decision-making.

principles.name: Equitable and Accessible
principles.description: We are committed to ensuring equitable access to AI education and resources for all students, educators, and families, regardless of background or circumstance.
commitments: Actively work to bridge the digital divide and eliminate barriers to AI literacy
Ensure AI benefits all members of our community
Strive to mitigate bias and discrimination in AI systems, promoting inclusive and culturally responsive AI applications

principles.name: Ethical and Transparent
principles.description: We will prioritize ethical considerations in the design, development, and implementation of AI systems, ensuring fairness, legitimacy, honesty, impartiality, transparency, and accountability.
commitments: Promote responsible data practices, adhering to privacy-by-design principles
Protect the privacy and security of student and staff information
Ensure users are informed when interacting with AI-enabled systems
Explain how AI arrived at its results and the reasoning behind them where appropriate
Monitor AI system behavior to prevent unintended consequences
Foster collaboration among students, educators, staff, families, and the community

principles.name: Human-Centered and Socially Beneficial
principles.description: We will leverage AI to personalize learning experiences, empower students, and foster critical thinking, while ensuring AI augments rather than replaces educators.
commitments: Ensure AI solutions support human goals with human needs in mind
Maintain human oversight of AI systems with options for human intervention
Consider broader societal impact of AI
Empower students to become informed and responsible citizens in an AI-powered world

principles.name: Continuous Improvement and Innovation
principles.description: We will foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement, encouraging experimentation and exploration of AI's potential to enhance teaching and learning.
commitments: Remain adaptable and responsive to the evolving AI landscape
Integrate new technologies and best practices as they emerge
Collaborate with external partners including universities, research institutions, EdTech nonprofits, and industry leaders

principles.name: Accountable and Sustainable
principles.description: We will establish clear lines of accountability for the development, deployment, and use of AI systems.
commitments: Ensure ethical conduct in AI behavior and take responsibility for addressing potential issues
Implement robust testing and monitoring programs
Recognize the environmental impact of AI models and actively seek ways to reduce negative effects such as excessive energy and water consumption

topics.name: AI Literacy
topics.content: AI Literacy represents a comprehensive understanding of AI's capabilities, limitations, ethical implications, and societal impact.

pillars.name: Foundational Knowledge
pillars.description: Understanding core AI concepts, terminology, and different types of AI technologies.

pillars.name: Practical Application
pillars.description: Developing the skills to effectively and responsibly use AI tools, including how to evaluate and integrate them into workflows.

pillars.name: Ethical Awareness
pillars.description: Recognizing the ethical considerations including bias, fairness, transparency, data privacy, and AI's impact on society.

pillars.name: Critical Thinking
pillars.description: Developing the ability to critically analyze AI-generated information, evaluate its reliability, understand its limitations, and mitigate potential risks.

pillars.name: Future-Oriented Perspective
pillars.description: Understanding the evolving nature of AI and its potential to shape the future of education and society by developing a growth mindset and a willingness to adapt.

why_it_matters.explanation: Students must develop critical thinking and digital literacy skills to effectively evaluate and utilize AI-generated content, while teachers need to adapt their pedagogical approaches to purposefully integrate AI into their lessons.

AI is causing significant changes in the job market, making AI literacy an essential skill for the future workforce. Traditional job roles are increasingly being transformed by the integration of AI tools and technologies.
AI is increasingly prevalent in our daily lives. It is essential to cultivate information literacy that encompasses AI, enabling us to critically evaluate and utilize AI-generated content.

AI has the potential to both exacerbate and alleviate existing educational inequities. Access to AI tools and training must be universal, ensuring all students have the opportunity to develop crucial AI literacy skills.

topics.name: AI Basics
topics.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) leverages computing power to mimic human cognitive functions such as problem-solving and decision-making. Generative AI (GenAI) is a subset of artificial intelligence that generates new content—including text, audio, code, images, or videos—based on vast amounts of training data.

key_concepts.definition: Technology that leverages computing power to mimic human cognitive functions such as problem-solving and decision-making, including learning from data, human feedback, and recognizing patterns through machine learning.
A subset of AI that generates new content—including text, audio, code, images, or videos—based on vast amounts of training data derived from the internet.
Inputs or queries submitted to a GenAI model to request and refine specific content.

Developing and deploying AI technologies with a steadfast commitment to fairness, transparency, and accountability, ensuring that they positively impact society. This is crucial, as biases in AI training data can inadvertently perpetuate discrimination.
False or misleading information produced by GenAI models that appears correct at first glance. Such outputs require careful review to prevent the dissemination of misleading information.

tool_categories.description: Freely available to anyone on the internet (e.g., ChatGPT).
Restricted to specific users within an organization or domain (e.g., Google's Gemini Enterprise).
Third-party providers requiring usage and data handling governed by strict contracts (e.g., Aleks).

sections.name: GenAI Guidance
sections.summary: Specific guidance for all stakeholders including students, parents, educators, administrators, ITS, and vendors.

topics.name: General Guidance for All Stakeholders
topics.content: Essential guidelines that apply to everyone in the CPS community when using GenAI tools.

subtopics.name: Privacy, Security, and Confidentiality
subtopics.content: When using GenAI tools, any information provided could potentially be used by companies to train their models. Assume that all information shared with a GenAI application will be used to train the model and could become accessible in the public domain.
recommendations: Always inform others when using GenAI tools that may impact their data and request their permission before doing so (e.g., meeting notetakers)
Never input personally identifiable information or protected health information into GenAI tools
Never input confidential, sensitive or legally protected information into GenAI tools
Never input copyrighted material or proprietary CPS intellectual property into GenAI tools
Staff: Contact your manager or the IT Service Desk at (773) 553-3925 if you are unsure whether information you are planning to input falls into any of the above categories

subtopics.name: Verification of the GenAI Tool's Output
subtopics.content: GenAI tools generate outputs based on their training from large and diverse data sets, which may include publicly available information. These outputs can contain fictitious elements (hallucinations) and may inadvertently include copyrighted or proprietary content.
recommendations: Always verify the accuracy and appropriateness of GenAI content before sharing
Avoid using any GenAI outputs that might contain copyrighted material without clear ownership

subtopics.name: Bias and Fairness
subtopics.content: AI models reflect the biases present in their training data, which can lead to outputs that unintentionally perpetuate stereotypes or discrimination.
recommendations: Conduct thorough reviews to ensure outputs are accurate and free of unintended biases
Verify and assess the source information that GenAI outputs are relying upon
Be vigilant of biases in GenAI outputs, particularly when used for decision-making or data analysis
Contact the Office of Equity at equity@cps.edu for support in determining if GenAI outputs are demonstrating bias

subtopics.name: Approved Tools and Permissions
subtopics.content: Approved GenAI tools can be found in the Ed Tech Catalog. Access to GenAI tools is governed by all relevant federal, state, and local laws (FERPA, COPPA, SOPPA, etc.), along with District policy.
recommendations: Under SOPPA, all educational technology tools, including those that leverage GenAI, are reviewed, approved, and listed in the CPS Ed Tech Catalog
Parents and guardians must consent for their child to use specific GenAI tools through individual school opt-out practices
Schools are encouraged to use or adapt an existing opt-out form if one already exists

topics.name: Guidance for Students
topics.content: Clear guidelines to ensure students uphold CPS values when using AI.

subtopics.name: Approved Tools and Permissions
recommendations: Students may only use GenAI tools that have been vetted and approved by CPS, as reflected in the CPS Ed Tech Catalog

A GenAI tool's approval within the Ed Tech Catalog reflects that it meets the District's standards for privacy, security, and confidentiality—but does not reflect it meets academic standards for verification, bias, or fairness
Students must obtain permission from their teacher before using GenAI tools to complete any assignment

subtopics.name: Academic Integrity
subtopics.content: While responsible GenAI use can assist in learning, students should submit work that is fundamentally their own.
recommendations: Students should clearly identify any AI-generated content used in their assignments
Students are required to cite the use of GenAI in their academic work and specify how they used it
Failing to cite GenAI use will be considered a violation of the Student Code of Conduct
review_process: Gathering information about the suspected incident, including providing the student an opportunity to explain
Making reasonable efforts to contact parents/guardians to discuss the incident before assigning consequences
Determining consequences based on the needs and rights of all parties

subtopics.name: Ethical Use and Digital Citizenship
recommendations: Students must use GenAI tools ethically
Students should never use GenAI tools to create inappropriate or harmful content
Students must follow the Student Acceptable Use Policy whenever they use GenAI tools
Violations may result in disciplinary actions ranging from a warning to more severe penalties

examples: Use GenAI as a brainstorming partner
Summarize ideas expressed during a small group discussion
Generate timelines and task lists for group projects
Synthesize a variety of opinions and propose compromise solutions
Use GenAI image creators to bring ideas to life
Create digital media such as videos and music with GenAI-powered design tools
Overcome writer's block by suggesting a variety of ideas and writing prompts
Ask GenAI to propose unconventional solutions to problems
Generate extra practice questions and study guides to review content
Use GenAI as an interactive tutor
Use generative search engines like Perplexity as a research assistant to gather, summarize, and cite information efficiently
Generate immediate feedback on first drafts of written assignments

subtopics.name: Monitoring and Consequences
subtopics.content: Usage of GenAI tools will be governed under the SOPPA model, wherein teachers are responsible for monitoring student use of approved technologies. Misuse of GenAI tools will be addressed in accordance with the Student Acceptable Use Policy and CPS' Student Code of Conduct.

topics.name: Guidance for Parents & Guardians
topics.content: AI tools are rapidly evolving, offering both opportunities and challenges for students. CPS is committed to integrating these tools in ways that prioritize student safety, academic integrity, and responsible use.

subtopics.name: Overview
subtopics.content: Teachers are being trained to incorporate GenAI tools into instruction effectively, ensuring they enhance learning while maintaining academic rigor. CPS values open communication and collaboration, encouraging parents and guardians to engage in meaningful conversations with their children and teachers about the use of GenAI in education.
recommendations: Engage in meaningful conversations with your children about GenAI use in education
Communicate with teachers about how GenAI is being used in the classroom
Share your insights, questions, and concerns as CPS navigates this evolving landscape

subtopics.name: Age-Appropriate and Approved Tools
subtopics.content: CPS staff ensure that students use GenAI tools that are appropriate for their age and maturity level. Teachers will adhere to age restrictions and only use tools suitable for students.
recommendations: CPS rigorously evaluates all educational technology tools—only tools meeting strict standards for data privacy, security, and confidentiality are approved for use
The CPS Ed Tech Catalog provides a comprehensive list of vetted tools with details about their data privacy practices
Visit the CPS Ed Tech Catalog for information about approved GenAI tools

subtopics.name: Responsible Use and Academic Integrity
subtopics.content: CPS expects students to produce original work and properly acknowledge any use of AI. Misrepresenting AI-generated work as one's own is considered a violation of academic integrity.
recommendations: CPS promotes responsible digital citizenship and ethical behavior when using GenAI tools
Students are expected to respect copyright laws, avoid plagiarism, and refrain from generating inappropriate or harmful content
Violations will be addressed in accordance with the Student Acceptable Use Policy and Student Code of Conduct
Discussing these principles with your children can help foster a strong sense of accountability and responsible online behavior

subtopics.name: Opt-Out Options
subtopics.content: Schools will clearly communicate information about the GenAI tools used in classrooms and the procedures for opting out if you prefer your child not use them.
recommendations: Schools are encouraged to use or adapt an existing opt-out form
A sample form that can be customized has been provided by CPS
Your participation in this process helps ensure that your child's educational experience aligns with your family's values and preferences

topics.name: Guidance for Educators & Staff
topics.content: As educators and staff at CPS, GenAI tools present an opportunity to elevate educational delivery and streamline administrative tasks.

subtopics.name: Ethical and Responsible Use
recommendations: Maintain transparency by appropriately citing or disclosing the use of GenAI
Ensure content generated is suitable for educational purposes
Staff must not enter confidential data into GenAI tools, including student record information and identifying information
Turn off chat history and data training in the settings of any GenAI tool used in professional practice

subtopics.name: Tool Approval and Use
recommendations: Use only GenAI tools that have been vetted and approved by CPS, as reflected in the CPS Ed Tech Catalog
Refer to the badges associated with each tool to understand when a tool may not meet academic standards

subtopics.name: Age Appropriate Usage
subtopics.content: GenAI tools set age restrictions in their Privacy Policy or Terms and Conditions. Review the terms before encouraging students to interact with any tools.

age_restrictions.parental_consent: Parental consent must be obtained for students

subtopics.name: Monitoring Student Use
subtopics.content: Staff using GenAI tools with students are responsible for ensuring that students engage responsibly. GenAI detection software should be used with caution.
recommendations: Maintain awareness of age limitations and permissions
Clearly communicate expectations to students and families
Report instances of misuse to their principal or designee
Develop alternate activities for students who lose GenAI access or whose families do not consent
Use AI detection software with caution—it can produce false positives and disproportionately flag work by English Learners
Prioritize holistic assessment of student work over relying solely on GenAI detection software

subtopics.name: Opportunities to Incorporate GenAI in the Classroom
subtopics.note: Going forward, this guide will be updated to include new tools, updated age appropriate guidelines, and examples within the District's Skyline curriculum of activities that demonstrate this shift.

examples.subject: Literacy
examples.without_genai: Students complete a character analysis after reading a book
examples.with_genai: After reading a book, the teacher uses GenAI to create an interactive character persona and conducts a teacher-led, whole-class 'interview' where students can ask questions about the character's motivations and feelings during the story.

examples.subject: Math
examples.without_genai: Teacher uses generic word problems provided by the curriculum for all students
examples.with_genai: Teacher creates customized word problems tailored to the current unit of study and individual students' unique needs and interests for intervention and continuing practice.

examples.subject: Science
examples.without_genai: Students research an animal species and create a poster or presentation using images from the internet
examples.with_genai: Students create prompts describing the habitat, diet, and survival adaptations of an animal species, which the teacher inputs into an AI image generator to create visuals for posters or presentations. Students evaluate the accuracy of the images.

examples.subject: Social Science
examples.without_genai: Students watch videos and complete worksheets about the role of community leaders
examples.with_genai: Students take on the roles of civic leaders and participate in a teacher-led discussion in which an AI chatbot is prompted to ask students age-appropriate questions about how they would set up an ideal community.

examples.subject: Literacy
examples.without_genai: Students use background knowledge to make inferences about characters' points of view
examples.with_genai: Students use GenAI under teacher supervision to explore point of view by generating descriptions of the plot from various characters and comparing/contrasting them in small group discussions.

examples.subject: Math
examples.without_genai: Teacher manually designs and delivers interventions for individual students
examples.with_genai: Students engage with GenAI tutors under teacher supervision to target and strengthen developing skills.

examples.subject: Science
examples.without_genai: Teacher gathers materials and sets up physical lab equipment for experiments
examples.with_genai: Under supervision, students use GenAI to carry out virtual experiments, hypothesizing and testing outcomes without physical lab equipment.

examples.subject: Social Science
examples.without_genai: Students write a report about their cultural heritage
examples.with_genai: Students work under teacher supervision with an AI image generator to create and critique images reflecting their personal cultural heritage, shared in presentations or multimedia projects.

examples.subject: Literacy
examples.without_genai: Students must wait for teacher feedback before revising an essay or report
examples.with_genai: Students use GenAI independently to receive instant feedback on the first draft of an essay or report, allowing them to immediately revise their work.

examples.subject: Math
examples.without_genai: Students are exposed to limited descriptions of complex mathematical concepts in a lecture or textbook
examples.with_genai: Students use GenAI tools independently to explore advanced mathematical concepts and ask questions until they achieve understanding.

examples.subject: Science
examples.without_genai: Students spend weeks conducting research projects and physical experiments
examples.with_genai: Teachers facilitate unsupervised use of GenAI by students to conduct in-depth research, utilizing AI to quickly gather data, analyze results, and simulate experiments.

examples.subject: Social Science
examples.without_genai: Students conduct internet research on current events
examples.with_genai: Students independently use a generative search engine to conduct an in-depth analysis of current events, exploring a variety of perspectives and synthesizing these into a presentation or debate.

topics.name: Guidance for Administrators
topics.content: As leaders within Chicago Public Schools, administrators play a critical role in overseeing the use and governance of Generative AI tools.

subtopics.name: Enforcement and Oversight
subtopics.content: Administrators are responsible for ensuring that staff and students comply with CPS's GenAI guidelines, taking an active role in enforcing guidelines and addressing deviations promptly.

subtopics.name: Incident Management
subtopics.content: Administrators must be prepared to respond swiftly to any incidents of misuse or breach of GenAI guidelines, including investigating the issue, understanding the impact, and taking appropriate action.
recommendations: Develop and maintain clear channels for reporting concerns or incidents related to GenAI use
Ensure that staff and students are aware of how and when to report issues

subtopics.name: Support and Resources
subtopics.content: Ensure that staff have the necessary resources and training to use GenAI tools effectively and responsibly, including facilitating ongoing professional development and access to the latest educational technologies.

topics.name: Guidance for ITS
topics.content: Essential to follow standard software engineering best practices to minimize potential bias and ensure data quality in GenAI models.

subtopics.name: Design and Development
recommendations: Ensure all software is secure by design, free from vulnerabilities, and continuously evaluated
Maintain AI software in a secure, private script repository with version control

subtopics.name: Deployment
recommendations: Test AI software in QA & development environment before production deployment
Implement continuous integration (CI) and continuous deployment (CD) when possible

callouts.label: Incident
callouts.content: All AI software and applications in the production environment must follow incident management protocols to handle any issues that arise.

subtopics.name: Management
subtopics.content: Ensure that staff have the necessary resources and training to use GenAI tools effectively and responsibly. This includes facilitating ongoing professional development and access to the latest educational technologies.

callouts.label: Vulnerability
callouts.content: Regularly update AI software according to patching standards and adhere to the change management process for any changes.

callouts.label: Configuration
callouts.content: Maintain AI software within a configuration management system (CMS), which includes details on software versions, relationships to other configuration items, and their locations.

subtopics.name: Monitoring and Noncompliance
subtopics.content: CPS reserves the right to access and monitor the use of AI applications on any CPS-issued devices or CPS-managed networks. Users who fail to comply may be subject to discipline up to and including termination.

topics.name: Guidance for Vendors
topics.content: Expectations and guidelines for third-party vendors providing AI and GenAI tools and services to CPS.

subtopics.name: Tool Approval and Integration
subtopics.content: All AI EdTech tools must undergo the same rigorous vetting and approval process (EdTech Request for Qualifications) before they can be used by students or with student data.
recommendations: Vendors must provide comprehensive documentation regarding data privacy practices
Vendors should provide information regarding age appropriateness of their tools

subtopics.name: Privacy, Security, and Confidentiality
recommendations: Ensure AI tools protect the privacy and security of all CPS stakeholders
No PII or protected health information should be collected, stored, or processed against CPS guidelines
Stakeholder information must not be used to train vendor models without explicit permission
Implement robust security measures following security by design principles

subtopics.name: Ethical and Responsible Use
recommendations: Develop and deploy AI with commitment to fairness, transparency, and accountability
Minimize potential bias in AI models
Address hallucinations with mitigation mechanisms
Strive for explainable AI with human-in-the-loop approach

subtopics.name: Support and Collaboration
recommendations: Provide adequate support and resources to CPS staff for the effective and responsible use of their AI tools, including training materials, technical support, and ongoing updates
Maintain open communication channels with CPS to address any concerns, issues, or updates related to their AI offerings
Collaborate with CPS on professional development initiatives related to their specific tools

sections.name: Approved Generative AI Tools
sections.summary: Approved GenAI tools can be found in the Ed Tech Catalog.

topics.name: Ed Tech Catalog
topics.content: Approved GenAI tools can be found in the Ed Tech Catalog. All tools undergo the EdTech Request for Qualifications (RFQ) process to ensure they meet CPS standards for privacy, security, and confidentiality.

sections.name: Professional Development
sections.summary: Badge pathways and Professional Learning Communities for AI skill development.

topics.name: Badge Pathway
topics.content: The AI Badge Pathway is a structured program designed to deepen understanding of AI and its practical applications within CPS.

badges.name: AI Foundations Badge
badges.description: Starting with foundational AI principles, emphasizing ethical considerations, bias awareness, and responsible data practices.

badges.name: AI Explorer Badge
badges.description: Guides participants to select appropriate AI tools based on their needs and desired outcomes.

badges.name: AI Innovator Badge
badges.description: Participants learn to develop AI-driven solutions for their unique challenges, aligning with CPS' strategic goals.
badges.prerequisites: AI Explorer Badge + AI Foundations Badge

topics.name: Professional Learning Communities (PLCs)
topics.content: AI Professional Learning Communities are collaborative groups where educators and staff learn, integrate, and grow with AI tools.
features: Continuous Support: Ensures ongoing support for educators as AI tools evolve
Digital Communities: Leverages digital platforms to foster shared knowledge and collective problem-solving
Monthly Webinars: Offers monthly webinar-style training sessions to introduce new AI developments
topics.prerequisite: Completion of the CPS AI Foundations Badge

sections.name: Conclusion
sections.summary: CPS is committed to fully integrating GenAI responsibly, maintaining open dialogue, and evolving policies to reflect collective experiences.

topics.name: Conclusion
topics.content: CPS is committed to fully integrating GenAI for the 2025-2026 school year. Our implementation of GenAI is guided by a commitment to ethical use, responsible innovation, and the continuous improvement of our educational practices. As we move forward, we will maintain an open dialogue within our school community, ensuring that our policies evolve to reflect our collective experiences and the ever-changing landscape of educational technology.

sections.name: Appendix
sections.summary: Steering committee members, subcommittees, glossary of AI terms, and version history.

topics.name: Steering Committee & Subcommittees
topics.content: The educational landscape is rapidly evolving, and CPS is committed to equipping our students and staff with the tools and knowledge to thrive in the age of AI. To guide this effort, CPS has established an AI Steering Committee, a cross-governing body that meets bi-weekly to ensure a holistic and equitable approach to GenAI across the District.

terms.definition: A set of step-by-step instructions that a computer follows to complete a task.
The potential for AI systems to perpetuate or amplify existing biases due to biased training data or flawed algorithms, resulting in unfair or discriminatory outcomes.
The ability of a computer or machine to mimic human intelligence (e.g., learn, reason, solve problems).
Guidelines for developing and using AI in a responsible and ethical way, ensuring fairness, safety, and respect for everyone.
The knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to interact with AI in a safe and effective way.
A computer program trained on a dataset to recognize patterns and perform specific tasks.
Measures taken to ensure AI systems are used in ways that prevent harm to individuals or society.
AI-powered software that can automate or assist users with a variety of tasks (e.g., writing assistants, tutoring programs, assessment tools).
When an AI system unfairly favors certain groups or produces results that are prejudiced, often because the training data is incomplete or reflects existing biases.
A prompting strategy that asks an AI tool to think step-by-step, which can produce better results for logical and mathematical reasoning tasks.
Information, such as facts, numbers, and text, that is used to train AI systems.
A large collection of organized information (like text, images, or numbers) used to train an AI model.
Protecting the personally identifiable information (PII) of students, teachers, and families when using digital tools, including AI tools.
Responsible and ethical use of technology, encompassing online safety, privacy, critical thinking, and respectful interactions in the digital world.
AI systems designed in a way that allows students and educators to understand how they work and how decisions are made.
A prompting strategy that includes two or more examples of the desired input and output.
A type of AI that can create new content, such as text, images, music, or code.
Any inaccurate or misleading output from an AI tool. These can be presented as facts by the AI tool, elevating the need to properly vet the outputs.
An understanding that humans should always be involved in the AI process, providing guidance, feedback, or making final decisions to ensure AI is used responsibly.
AI tools restricted for use within a specific organization or domain, which may require payment (e.g., Google's Gemini Enterprise).
An AI model trained on large amounts of text to identify patterns between words, concepts, and phrases in order to generate effective responses to prompts.
A subset of AI focused on developing computer programs that can analyze data to make decisions or predictions.
A field of AI that enables machines to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
A prompting strategy that includes one example of the desired input and output.
The information or creative work that an AI tool produces after it is prompted, such as an answer, text summary, image, or music.
The method for interacting with an AI tool in the form of a request, question, snippet, or an example.
Tools available for anyone to use on the internet, such as Gemini Chat, ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity.
A type of machine learning that provides feedback to a program to improve its decisions over time.
A type of ML that uses labeled datasets to train a program to recognize patterns in data.
Being open and honest about how AI systems are trained and how they work, including being clear about when and how AI is used in the classroom.
A type of ML that uses unlabeled datasets to allow a program to identify patterns in data without a specific output in mind.
GenAI provided by third-party vendors which CPS may contract with to ensure data handling and usage align with District standards and policies.
A prompting strategy that doesn't include any examples about the desired input and output.
